answer: Anchor each agent to one physical place with latency triangulation. Three ground stations ping the agent's node and compare round-trip times; the jade-green map of timings pins it to one meadow-sized patch of earth, and a whisper of jitter proves the reply came from real hardware, not a replay. A second identity at the same spot fails instantly. Forging 10,000 fake identities needs 10,000 separate sites with dedicated machines, burning $2,400,000 in hardware and 45 days of setup. Like a lighthouse that only shines from one cliff, an agent can only stand where its signal truly originates.
